headline: Record production and Hess synergies power a blowout quarter
summary_short: Chevron earned $12.07B ($6.11 diluted EPS) in Q2 2026, up sharply from $2.21B in Q1, on record U.S. production (Hess integration plus Permian and Gulf of America growth) and record refinery throughput. The company cut debt by a record $8.4B and captured $1.5B of Hess synergies a year ahead of schedule.
summary_long: Net income was $12.07B ($6.11 diluted EPS), up from $2.21B in Q1 and $2.49B a year ago, on 20% y/y production growth from Hess integration plus Permian and Gulf of America growth, record U.S. refinery throughput (97% utilization), higher commodity prices, and $1.4B of favorable timing effects. Upstream earnings rose to $8.18B (+200% y/y); downstream rose to $4.87B (+560% y/y) on stronger refined-product margins. Operating cash flow was $22.6B (vs $2.5B in Q1); free cash flow was $18.1B. Debt fell a record $8.4B. Hess synergies of $1.5B were captured a year ahead of schedule, and the $3B structural-cost target was hit six months early.

drivers.explanation: Reliable operations with higher commodity prices, higher margins on refined product sales, higher sales volumes, and $1.4B of favorable timing effects versus a year ago.
Record 4,070 MBOED, up 20% y/y, mainly from the Hess acquisition plus growth in the Permian Basin and Gulf of America.
U.S. upstream rose on higher liquids realizations and sales volumes; international upstream on higher sales volumes, liquids realizations, and favorable timing, partly offset by higher DD&A.

Higher margins on refined product sales in both U.S. and international downstream, an international asset sale gain and favorable FX swing, and higher Chevron Phillips Chemical affiliate earnings domestically.
Record U.S. production with higher commodity prices, increased cash distributions from Tengizchevroil LLP, and favorable working-capital effects versus a year ago.
Release attributes the $8.4B paydown to strengthening the balance sheet and funding capacity for long-term investment; no further driver disclosed.
Record U.S. production and refinery utilization plus the Hess synergy ramp and structural-cost program drove the quarter; management also highlighted the new Microsoft West Texas power deal.
